pharm: Antithrombin-dependent inhibitor of factor Xa (and, less so, thrombin), derived by peroxide depolymerization of porcine heparin
quick: 50 anti-Xa units/kg subcutaneously every 12 hours (knee replacement prophylaxis)
LMWHs generally preferred anticoagulants; ardeparin-specific data limited
Milk excretion poorly characterized; LMWHs generally low risk
Accumulates in renal impairment - increased bleeding risk; use caution
Platelet count (HIT), signs of bleeding; anti-Xa in special cases
summary: Ardeparin (Normiflo) was a low molecular weight heparin used for prevention of deep-vein thrombosis after total knee replacement surgery. It is an antithrombin-dependent inhibitor of factor Xa and, to a lesser extent, thrombin, derived from porcine intestinal heparin, with an anti-Xa to anti-IIa ratio of roughly 2:1. The labeled regimen was 50 anti-Xa units/kg subcutaneously every 12 hours, started postoperatively and continued for up to about 14 days or until discharge. It was voluntarily WITHDRAWN from the US market in March 2000 for commercial (not safety or efficacy) reasons and is not currently available. Like all LMWHs its main risks are bleeding and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), and it accumulates in renal failure. This record is provided for historical reference.
indications: Historical: prevention of deep-vein thrombosis/venous thromboembolism following total knee replacement surgery (withdrawn)

dosage.r: DVT prophylaxis after total knee replacement
dosage.d: 50 anti-Xa units/kg subcutaneously every 12 hours (about 0.005 mL/kg)
dosage.n: Started postoperatively (about 12-24 h after surgery), continued up to ~14 days or until discharge

admin: Administer by deep subcutaneous injection; not for intramuscular use
Begin postoperatively (about 12-24 hours after surgery) per the historical regimen
Continue for up to about 14 days or until discharge
Monitor platelet count for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
Avoid neuraxial (spinal/epidural) procedures around dosing because of spinal hematoma risk
Not currently available - withdrawn from the US market in 2000
moa: Ardeparin binds antithrombin III, accelerating the inactivation of clotting factor Xa and, to a lesser degree, thrombin (factor IIa); it also binds heparin cofactor II. Because LMWH chains are shorter than unfractionated heparin, anti-Xa activity predominates over anti-IIa activity (anti-Xa:anti-IIa ratio about 2:1, versus about 1:1 for unfractionated heparin). The net effect is reduced thrombin generation and clot formation, providing predictable anticoagulation suitable for fixed weight-based prophylactic dosing.

absolute: Known or history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
Hypersensitivity to ardeparin, heparin, porcine products, or parabens (preservative)
relative: Recent CNS, eye or major surgery; brain tumor or aneurysm
Renal or hepatic impairment; neuraxial anesthesia
monitor: Signs of bleeding (CBC/hematocrit, stool occult blood)
Anti-factor Xa levels in renal failure, obesity or pregnancy

preg: As a class, LMWHs do not appreciably cross the placenta and are generally the preferred anticoagulants in pregnancy. Ardeparin-specific pregnancy data are limited and the exact original pregnancy category is not reliably documented; historical labeling advised informing the prescriber of pregnancy or planned pregnancy.
lact: Excretion of ardeparin into human milk is poorly characterized. LMWHs are generally regarded as low risk during breastfeeding because of minimal oral bioavailability in the infant, but ardeparin-specific data are lacking.
renal: LMWHs are cleared renally and accumulate in renal impairment, increasing bleeding risk; kidney disease was listed as a precaution. No specific creatinine-clearance threshold for ardeparin was published; class-level caution and anti-Xa monitoring would apply in renal failure.
hepatic: Liver disease was listed as a precaution because of bleeding risk. No specific hepatic dose-adjustment regimen for ardeparin was published.

major: Other anticoagulants (warfarin, heparin) - increased bleeding risk
moderate: Antiplatelet agents (aspirin, clopidogrel, ticlopidine, dipyridamole, cilostazol) - increased bleeding risk
Antiplatelet-effect herbals (fish oil, garlic, ginger, ginkgo, feverfew) - increased bleeding risk
interactions.alcohol: No ardeparin-specific interaction documented; alcohol can compound bleeding risk, especially with liver disease or GI ulcers.
interactions.diagnostics: Routine coagulation monitoring is generally not required for fixed-dose prophylaxis; anti-factor Xa levels are used in special populations. Monitor platelet count for HIT.

serious: Major hemorrhage (GI bleed, hematuria, intracranial or retroperitoneal bleeding)
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), which can paradoxically cause thrombosis
emergency: Signs of thrombosis from HIT (chest pain, limb swelling/warmth)
Spinal/epidural hematoma (back pain, leg weakness, bladder/bowel dysfunction)

monitoring: Platelet count for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (suspect a fall of 30% or more, typically days 4-14)
Signs and symptoms of bleeding; CBC/hematocrit and stool occult blood as indicated
Anti-factor Xa levels in renal failure, obesity or pregnancy
Neurologic status when neuraxial anesthesia is used
counsel: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin to prevent blood clots after surgery
Report unusual or heavy bleeding, black stools, blood in urine, or large bruises
Tell all clinicians you are on an anticoagulant before any procedure or new medicine
Avoid other blood thinners and anti-inflammatory painkillers unless your doctor approves
Seek urgent care for severe back pain or leg weakness if you have had spinal anesthesia
pk: Anticoagulant (anti-Xa) effect develops after subcutaneous absorption
Peak anti-Xa activity about 2-3 hours after a subcutaneous dose
Anti-Xa half-life about 3.3 hours; anti-IIa about 1.2 hours
Anti-Xa activity persists about 12 hours, supporting twice-daily dosing
Store at room temperature (about 15-25 C); protect from light/heat/moisture; do not freeze
pearls: WITHDRAWN from the US market in March 2000 for commercial reasons (not safety/efficacy) - not currently available
A low molecular weight heparin with predictable response and fixed weight-based dosing; routine lab monitoring usually unnecessary
Monitor for HIT (platelet count fall, typically days 4-14)
Accumulates in renal failure - increased bleeding risk
Porcine-derived - contraindicated in pork/heparin hypersensitivity; anti-Xa:anti-IIa ratio about 2:1
missed: Give the missed dose when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it - do not double up. (Ardeparin is no longer marketed.)
overdose: Overdose manifests as bleeding. Protamine sulfate only partially reverses LMWH anti-Xa activity (it more completely neutralizes anti-IIa); historical labeling suggested about 1 mg protamine sulfate per 100 anti-Xa units. Provide supportive care and transfusion as needed for serious bleeding.
